title: nonlocal Keyword: Fixing Enclosing Scope Mutation
description: make_counter_broken fails with UnboundLocalError because assignment to count makes Python treat count as local to inc, but count is read before assignment. make_counter_fixed uses nonlocal count to declare count belongs to enclosing scope, allowing mutation. Fixed version increments and returns 1, 2, 3.
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: make_counter_broken: count = 0 in outer. inc() tries count = count + 1. Python sees assignment to count, marks count as local to inc. Reading count before assignment raises UnboundLocalError.
Assignment to count inside inc makes Python treat count as local to inc. The read of count on RHS happens before assignment, causing UnboundLocalError.
make_counter_fixed: same structure but inc() declares nonlocal count. This tells Python: count refers to the binding in the enclosing make_counter_fixed scope. Assignment mutates that binding.
nonlocal count declares count is in the enclosing function scope, not local to inc. Allows read and write to that binding.

steps.question: Why does make_counter_broken raise UnboundLocalError instead of NameError?
steps.answer: Because Python detects the assignment to count at compile time and marks count as local to inc. The error occurs at runtime when reading the local count before it has a value.

steps.description: Test: try/except catches UnboundLocalError from broken counter. Fixed counter called three times prints 1 2 3.
Output: Broken counter: cannot access local variable 'count' where it is not associated with a value
Output: 1 2 3  -  fixed counter increments correctly across calls.
